description: trunk-coverage.yml runs on every push to develop with cancel-in-progress (trunk-coverage.yml:3-12). Captured history holds 123 push runs from 2026-10-21 18:57 to 2026-10-24 16:07 (about 42.7 starts a day): 51 succeeded, 71 were cancelled and one was in progress, about 17.7 successful completions a day. Cancelled runs averaged 14.95 minutes from creation to final update; that is wall time, not runner occupancy. In the 40-run job sample, 14 completed producers averaged 40.18 runner-minutes and 20 cancelled runs that had jobs averaged 15.32 runner-minutes (five cancelled runs listed no jobs, and one run was monitor-only). Only three days of history exist, so every figure here is an estimate to be re-measured. The workflow runs the medium tier a third time per merge, instrumented, and occupies concurrency slots that PR CI waits for. It produces the coverage map that PR selection reads, but also publishes collection and shard evidence (30-day retention) and runs the staleness issue monitor; those must stay accounted for. DESIGN CHOICE: replace the push trigger with scheduled runs (proposal: six a day; the owner sets the cadence), keeping workflow_dispatch and the daily staleness job. A push guard (commit-distance) is not the chosen design; if the owner prefers it, the schedule-specific acceptance must be rewritten and it must be shown that skipped runs cannot crowd usable artifacts out of discovery. Scheduled maps are ignored today: PR selection trusts maps only from push and workflow_dispatch runs (scripts/coverage_test_selection.py:33, checked at :868 and :911), and every map-building job is skipped on schedule events (trunk-coverage.yml:21,73,168). Both must change. Two separate limits currently share the constant MAX_MAP_BEHIND_COMMITS = 50: artifact discovery searches only 50 workflow runs (:858-879) and selection allows at most 50 ancestor commits between the map and the PR base (:727-729); decide each limit separately. Map retention is seven days (trunk-coverage.yml:222-229). The staleness monitor queries only push runs (scripts/coverage_map_staleness.py:40-55) and treats a failed lookup as 'unknown', which opens no issue (:62-65, :173-188); both need change. fetch-map currently reports no producer run id (:951-978, :1033-1052). A new cron trigger needs owner approval before merge. Rough estimate: four to six successful producers a day cost about 161-241 runner-minutes against about 710-790 saved at the observed push rate, roughly 75-83%. A schedule is not a freshness guarantee: the captured merge history has 20 pushes in four hours and 24 in six hours. The repository is public, so GitHub-hosted runner minutes are free; the binding limit is the concurrency cap. Queue time and PR time-to-green are the primary success metrics, runner-minutes secondary.
